t: The Jurchens were culturally diverse: some groups lived as hunter-gatherers, some as semi-nomadic pastoralists and most as sedentary farmers.
Wanyan Aguda unified the Jurchen tribes in 1115 and founded the Jin dynasty, which conquered the Liao in 1125 and took the Song capital of Kaifeng in 1127 before falling to the Mongols in 1234.
Nurhaci, a Jianzhou chieftain, united the Jurchen tribes from 1586 and organised them into the Eight Banners, and his son Hong Taiji renamed the people Manchus in 1635.
dyk: The Jin dynasty's name means "gold" and comes from the "Gold River", Aisin in Manchu, in the Jurchens' ancestral homeland.
ev: The Jurchens first appear in Chinese records
Goryeo sends 170,000 soldiers against the Jurchens and builds the Nine Fortresses, later handed back
Wanyan Aguda unifies the Jurchen tribes and declares himself emperor of the Jin
Wanyan Xiyin invents the Jurchen script on Aguda's orders
The Jin capture the Song capital of Kaifeng in the Jingkang incident
Caizhou falls to the Mongols, ending the Jin dynasty
The Ming create the Nurgan Command Post at Telin on the lower Amur
Hong Taiji renames the Jurchens as Manchus

f.homeland: the forests and river valleys of Manchuria, in what is now China's Heilongjiang and Jilin provinces and Russia's Primorsky Krai; the Mudan River, the Changbai mountains, Liaodong, the Songhua and Amur rivers and the Yalu and Tumen borderlands
f.period: first in Chinese records in 748; vassals of the Liao dynasty by the 11th century; the Wanyan federation under Wugunai (1021–74); the Jin dynasty (1115–1234); Jianzhou, Haixi and Wild Jurchens under the Ming dynasty (1368–1644); unification under Nurhaci from 1586; renamed Manchus in 1635
f.known: the Jin dynasty and the capture of Kaifeng in 1127; the Jurchen script of 1120; the Eight Banners; the queue hairstyle; horsemanship, archery and hunting; trade in pearls and ginseng; founding the Qing dynasty
f.sources: Chinese records from 748, the History of Jin and the Ming Veritable Records; Korean accounts such as that of the emissary Sin Chung-il in 1595; the Yongning Temple steles at Telin in four languages; oral tradition of the Wanyan clan; a burial ground excavated by Russian archaeologists in Primorye in 2012; genetic studies of the Aisin Gioro
